facts.statement: Gilchristosuchus is an extinct genus of neosuchian crocodyliform named after the ranch owners where the type specimen was discovered.
facts.quote: Gilchristosuchus (meaning "Gilchrist [the owners of the ranch where the type specimen was found] crocodile") is an extinct genus of neosuchian crocodyliform.

facts.statement: Fossils of Gilchristosuchus were found in the upper Milk River Formation of Alberta, Canada, dating to the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Its fossils have been found in the upper Milk River Formation of Alberta, Canada, in rocks of either latest Santonian or earliest Campanian age (Late Cretaceous).

facts.statement: The genus Gilchristosuchus was described in 1993 by scientists Wu and Brinkman.
facts.quote: Gilchristosuchus was described in 1993 by Wu and Brinkman.

facts.statement: The type species is Gilchristosuchus palatinus, named for its distinctive palatine bones.
facts.quote: The type species is G. palatinus, in reference to its distinctive palatine bones.

facts.statement: The skull of Gilchristosuchus would have been approximately 15 cm long when complete.
facts.quote: The skull would have been about 15 cm long when complete.

facts.statement: Despite its small size, the skull ornamentation and bone fusion indicate that the specimen was an adult.
facts.quote: Although the specimen is not large, the ornamentation of the skull surfaces and bone fusion indicate it was an adult.

facts.statement: Researchers suggested that Gilchristosuchus was the most derived neosuchian crocodyliform that did not belong to Eusuchia, the group containing all living crocodilians.
facts.quote: Based on previous research, Wu and Brinkman suggested that their new genus was the most derived neosuchian that wasn't within Eusuchia, the group including all living crocodilians.

facts.statement: Gilchristosuchus belongs to the parent group Neosuchia.
Gilchristosuchus is classified within the class Reptilia.
Gilchristosuchus lived during the Santonian stage, between 85.7 and 83.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Santonian to Santonian (85.7 to 83.6 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The genus is based on fossil specimen RTMP 91.101.1, which consists of a partial posterior skull and a neck vertebra.
rejected.quote: Gilchristosuchus is based on RTMP 91.101.1, a partial posterior skull and a neck vertebra.
